topic: ECU tune alone on a factory-turbocharged petrol engine

cases.car: 2015 Ford Mustang EcoBoost (2.3L turbo I4; transmission not given in summary)
cases.change: SCT X4 Power Flash handheld, supplied 93-octane tune only, otherwise stock car
cases.measure: rear-wheel horsepower and torque, chassis dyno
cases.note: Summary: 'The stock car made 273.2 hp and 303.8 lb-ft at the rear wheels on a chassis dyno.' Quoted: 'Our stock 2015 EcoBoost, with only the supplied 93 octane tune put down 291.8 hp at 5,468 rpm and 339.9 lb-ft of torque at 3,114 rpm, to the rear wheels. That's a gain of 18.6 hp, and 36.1 lb-ft.' Also: at 3,600 rpm the tune had already picked up nearly 32 hp (mid-range gain larger than peak gain). Boost figures are the summary's approximations: 'Boost on the tuned pull climbed from 10 to about 25 psi, versus a stock peak of roughly 20 psi.' Read from search-result summary; page not opened. First-reader check note: Two separate searches agree: stated before figures plus the quoted after figures and stated gains are arithmetically consistent (291.8 - 273.2 = 18.6; 339.9 - 303.8 = 36.1). Boost psi values are approximate ('roughly', 'about') and should be weighted lightly.
cases.checkNote: Second-reader search (a combined query) did not return the Ford Muscle page, so the 273.2 -> 291.8 rwhp and 303.8 -> 339.9 lb-ft figures rest on the first reader's two agreeing summaries; nothing found contradicts them, and the approximate boost figures remain unverified.

cases.car: 2017 Ford Mustang EcoBoost (2.3L turbo I4; transmission not given in summary)
cases.change: COBB Accessport Stage 1 91-octane off-the-shelf map, reflash only, done first on a bone-stock car (intake and exhaust were tested afterwards, separately)
cases.measure: peak wheel horsepower and wheel torque, chassis dyno
cases.publisher: DSPORT Magazine (Test & Tune: 2017 Ford Mustang | Intake, Exhaust & Tune)
cases.note: Summary: 'Cobb Stage 1 tune alone (DSPORT): Stock output was 230.32 whp at 21 psi. After the reflash, output was 275.16 whp, and boost rose by about two psi to 22.93. Adding an intake brought it to 283.61 whp.' Second summary gives the rating: '310 horsepower at 5,500 RPM and 320 lb-ft of torque at 2,500 RPM (to the flywheel)' and the test plan: 'how an intake, exhaust, and a tune would affect a bone-stock Ford Mustang Ecoboost.' Wheel torque before/after was not in the first reader's summaries (added by the second reader, see below). Read from search-result summary; page not opened. First-reader check note: Dyno and boost figures come from one search summary; a second search confirmed the article, its stock rating and its bone-stock starting point but did not repeat the dyno numbers. Gain is +44.84 whp (+19.5%) for only +1.93 psi peak boost, so the tune also changed timing/boost curve, not just peak boost. Second reader: two further search summaries quote the article: 'The Mustang put down a peak 230.32whp and 275.49 lb-ft of torque when running at 21 psi of boost'; 'After a quick reflash, our Ecoboost Mustang delivered a peak 275.16whp and 345.41 lb-ft of torque. The map also raised the boost by two psi for a total of 22.93 psi'; and the article's own stated gain, 'a peak gain of 44.81whp (19.4-percent) and 69.91 lb-ft of torque (25-percent)' (arithmetic gives 44.84 whp and 69.92 lb-ft). The tester started with the Accessport and its Stage 1 91-octane pre-loaded map; wheel torque values were added from these summaries. Caveats: the 230.32 whp baseline is about 74% of the 310 hp crank rating (a low-reading dyno and/or a conservative stock calibration on the test fuel; the baseline fuel grade was not in the summaries), and COBB's own map notes quote 91-octane results against a 93-octane baseline, so this percentage is not comparable with COBB's published percentages. This is the largest EcoBoost gain on the page: S3 Magazine's car gained +9 whp / +40 lb-ft from the same tune family.
cases.checkNote: Second-reader searches repeated the article's stock baseline (230.32 whp / 275.49 lb-ft at 21 psi), the Stage 1 result (275.16 whp / 345.41 lb-ft at 22.93 psi) and its stated gain (44.81 whp, 69.91 lb-ft), with the reflash done first on the bone-stock car: one magazine test, wheel figures, one change.

cases.car: Ford Mustang EcoBoost (S550, 2.3L turbo I4; year and transmission not given in summary)
cases.change: COBB Accessport with COBB Stage 1 off-the-shelf tune only
cases.measure: wheel horsepower and wheel torque, chassis dyno
cases.note: Summary: 'S3mag reported that the car put down 221whp and 261wtq stock, and that with nothing but the COBB Accessport & COBB Stage-1 tune, it jumped to 230hp and 301wtq.' The after power is written '230hp' in context of wheel figures. Read from search-result summary; page not opened. First-reader check note: Single search summary. Shape matches the other EcoBoost cases: small peak-power gain (+9, +4%) but large torque gain (+40 lb-ft, +15%).
cases.checkNote: Two second-reader search summaries repeat the wording (221 whp / 261 wtq stock, then 230 hp / 301 wtq with 'nothing but' the COBB Accessport and Stage 1 tune), but the car's year, the dyno and the fuel are not given, it is not visible whether this was the magazine's own dyno session, and the +9 whp power gain is about a fifth of DSPORT's for the same tune family, so treat the power gain as dyno- and fuel-dependent.

cases.car: 2020 Toyota GR Supra (A90, 3.0L B58 turbo I6, automatic)
cases.change: EcuTek calibration by the tuning shop, 93-octane fuel (the shop describes the gain as coming 'from calibration alone')
cases.measure: wheel horsepower and wheel torque, shop chassis dyno, baseline pulls taken before the work
cases.note: Tuner's own result (the shop that wrote and sold the calibration). CORRECTED BY THE SECOND READER. As first written this case paired a baseline of 337.79 whp / 400.56 lb-ft with the 444.76 whp / 542.22 lb-ft result (gain +106.97 whp, +141.66 lb-ft); a site-restricted search showed those are two different cars. This page ('2020 Toyota GR Supra - EcuTek Tuned'), quoted in the search summary: 'With 93 octane in the tank, and 91° F ambient air temperature in the dyno room, [the tuner] was able to increase the B58's output to 444.76whp & 542.22lbft, holding 21psi to redline -- a gain of 107.90whp & 130.06lbft from calibration alone!', with a pre-work baseline of 336.86whp & 412.16lbft (444.76 - 336.86 = 107.90; 542.22 - 412.16 = 130.06). The 337.79whp & 400.56lbft baseline belongs to the shop's separate 'Downshift Blue 2020 Toyota GR Supra - EcuTek Tuned' page, where the car made 444.77whp & 528.79lbft (gain 106.98whp & 128.23lbft) at 98° F on 93 octane and 21 psi and is listed with an ETS down-pipe, HRE wheels and KW coilovers, so that car is not recorded as a tune-only case. Stock boost was not given; 21 psi is the tuned figure 'held to redline'. Other National Speed A90 results seen in summaries (not recorded): about 334 to about 458 whp with 23 psi held to redline; about 345 to about 419 whp on 92 octane; another stock baseline of 344.92whp & 388.35lbft. Corrected gain: +107.90 whp (+32.0%), +130.06 lb-ft (+31.6%). Read from search-result summaries; page not opened.
cases.checkNote: Corrected by the second reader: the first-written baseline (337.79 whp / 400.56 lb-ft) belongs to a different car on the shop's 'Downshift Blue' page (listed with a downpipe; 444.77 whp / 528.79 lb-ft), whereas this page's own baseline is 336.86 whp / 412.16 lb-ft and its stated gain of 107.90 whp / 130.06 lb-ft 'from calibration alone' matches the arithmetic; still a tuner's own dyno.

cases.car: Toyota GR Supra (A90, 3.0L B58 turbo I6; year and transmission not given in summary)
cases.change: VR Tuned ECU flash only, pump fuel
cases.measure: wheel horsepower and wheel torque, tuner's chassis dyno
cases.note: Tuner's own claim. Quoted: 'With the new VR Tuned flash installed, the A90 Supra put down 372whp and 429wtq, representing power gains of +62whp and +38lb-ft.' The before figures are the after figures minus the stated gains (372 - 62, 429 - 38); the stock run itself was not quoted. Summary adds that a 93-octane blend added a bit more. Read from search-result summary; page not opened. First-reader check note: Before values derived by subtraction from published after-and-gain figures, not printed directly. Stock baseline (310 whp) sits at the low end of the 310-345 whp range of stock A90 baselines across shops noted in the same summary.
cases.checkNote: Second-reader search (a combined query) returned no VR Tuned result, so the 372 whp / 429 wtq claim and the baseline obtained by subtraction rest on the first reader's single summary; the +62 whp claim is smaller than National Speed's calibration-only gain on the same engine (+107.90 whp), so its size is not contradicted.

cases.car: 2018 Honda Civic Type R (FK8, 2.0L turbo I4, manual)
cases.change: Hondata FlashPro reflash only; aftermarket intake and exhaust were swapped back to factory parts for this run
cases.measure: peak wheel horsepower and wheel torque, chassis dyno
cases.publisher: DSPORT Magazine (Test & Tune: 2018 Honda Civic Type R, Part 1)
cases.note: Quoted: 'With everything stock and just the reflash, the car delivered 314.15 peak whp and 332.27 lb-ft of peak torque.' And: 'On their Dyno, the Type R showed an impressive 293.25 peak whp, and a peak of 282.84 lb-ft of torque.' The results table lists the FlashPro run at 314.15 whp with a 20.90 whp gain. Read from search-result summary; page not opened. First-reader check note: Two searches agree and the table gain (20.90) matches 314.15 - 293.25. A separate DSPORT FK8 article gives a different stock baseline (296.72 whp / 290.63 lb-ft) and an off-the-shelf Hondata result of 318.88 whp / 334.96 lb-ft, but the summaries did not confirm that pair was the same car and day, so it is not recorded as a case. Gain here: +20.90 whp (+7.1%), +49.43 lb-ft (+17.5%).
cases.checkNote: Second-reader search did not return the Part 1 article (only DSPORT's later Type R fuel-system article appeared), so the 293.25 -> 314.15 whp and 282.84 -> 332.27 lb-ft figures rest on the first reader's two agreeing summaries and the table gain; nothing found contradicts them.

cases.car: 2019 Honda Civic Si (1.5L turbo I4, manual)
cases.change: Hondata FlashPro base map, 91-octane fuel (whether the article's MA Performance intake was already fitted for this run is unresolved)
cases.measure: peak wheel horsepower and wheel torque, chassis dyno
cases.publisher: DSPORT Magazine (Test & Tune: 2019 Honda Civic Si | Intake, Flashpro, Type R Clutch & E85)
cases.note: Summary: 'The Civic Si made 189.81 peak whp and 190.58 lb-ft of torque stock, running the factory 18.87 psi of boost. After a FlashPro base map on 91-octane, it reached a peak 203.88whp and 214.70 lb-ft of torque', with 'boost increasing to 22.49 psi'. Gain stated as 14.07 whp and 24.12 lb-ft. On E85 (gauge read 76 percent ethanol) the same car made 240.59 whp / 237.96 lb-ft. Read from search-result summary; page not opened. First-reader check note: Figures agree across two searches and the stated gains match the arithmetic. Unresolved: the article also fitted an MA Performance intake and the summaries could not say whether it was on the car for the 203.88 whp run. A separate DSPORT 1.5T Civic article reports about 187 whp at 18.55 psi rising to 212.65 whp at 25.56 psi with a custom FlashPro tune (not recorded; car model and mods unclear).
cases.checkNote: Second-reader search repeated only the stock baseline (189.81 whp / 190.58 lb-ft at 18.87 psi) and that a FlashPro base-map reflash was 'the next step', not the 203.88 whp / 214.70 lb-ft / 22.49 psi result or whether the MA Performance intake was already fitted, so a single change is not established.

cases.car: 2015 Volkswagen Golf R (US-spec, Mk7, 2.0T EA888, DSG)
cases.change: APR Stage I ECU software, 93 AKI fuel
cases.measure: instrumented acceleration (0-60 mph and quarter mile), tuner's own testing
cases.note: Tuner's own test. Quoted: '12.849 @ 105.300 MPH vs 11.956 @ 113.733 MPH - 1/4 Mile' and '0-60 MPH times were reduced to 3.8 seconds while the 30-130 MPH test was completed 5.9 seconds faster!' Table 0-60: 4.641 s stock vs 3.869 s Stage I; with 1-foot rollout 4.247 s vs 3.490 s. Read from search-result summary; page not opened. First-reader check note: Two searches agree on all figures. Manufacturer-sourced; the stock 12.849 s is quicker than The Drive's quoted 13.4 s stock Mk7 Golf R, so the baseline may be a well-launched or favourable-conditions run. Trap speed rose 8.43 mph (+8.0%). Second reader: NOT CHECKED. The six-search cap was reached before this case, so no check mark is set; it stands on the first reader's two summaries only.

cases.car: Volkswagen Golf R Mk8 (2.0T; year and transmission not given in summary)
cases.change: Racing Line power control module only (plug-in piggyback, not an ECU reflash; described as the equivalent of a Stage 1 tune because no reflash existed yet)
cases.measure: 0-60 mph and quarter mile, timed by an independent video channel, same car stock then with module
cases.publisher: TopSpeed (reporting an Awesome Cars video test; also covered by Formacar)
cases.note: Summary: 'The stock car ran 0-60 in 4.18 seconds and the quarter mile in 12.46 seconds. After a Racing Line power control module was added, it ran 0-60 in 4.07 seconds and the quarter mile in 12.28 seconds.' Quoted: 'at the point of filming the test, there was no tune available for the Golf R Mk8, so the PCM is, technically, the equivalent of a Stage 1 tune.' Read from search-result summary; page not opened. First-reader check note: Single search summary, two outlets cited. Piggyback module rather than reflash; trap speeds and power figures not given. Gain is much smaller than APR's Mk7 reflash result (-0.18 s vs -0.89 s quarter mile). Second reader: NOT CHECKED. The six-search cap was reached before this case, so no check mark is set; note that the change is a plug-in piggyback module, not an ECU reflash, so it sits at the edge of this page's topic.

cases.car: Volkswagen GTI Mk7 (2.0T EA888 Gen 3; year and transmission not given in summary), VWR intake fitted for both runs
cases.change: Unitronic Stage 1+ ECU software only (intake already fitted in the baseline run)
cases.publisher: Shop DAP (VW tuning shop that sells and installs the software)
cases.note: Shop's own reported result for software it sells. Quoted: 'MK7 VW GTI Stock (w/ MK7 GTI VWR Intake) Wheel Horsepower – 207, and MK7 VW GTI w/ Unitronic Stage 1 Plus Software Wheel Horsepower – 282.' Write-up gives the gain as 75 hp and 43 lb-ft; absolute torque values were not in the summary. Read from search-result summary; page not opened. First-reader check note: Single search summary. +75 whp (+36%) is the largest relative gain on this page and is a seller's figure. Grassroots Motorsports ran an independent 034Motorsport-tune Mk7 GTI dyno test at VMP Performance but its numbers were only in a chart not visible in summaries, so it is not recorded. Second reader: the search summary could not find the 207 / 282 whp figures or the 43 lb-ft gain. It found the shop's 'Part 13 (Tuning Software) of the DAP MK7 GTI Build' page, which says Stage 1+ with the VWR intake was dyno-tested and cites gains of +100hp and +89lbft (a crank-rated basis); the software maker's product page lists 'STOCK POWER: 210HP / 258LB-FT' against 'Stage 1+ : 310HP / 347LB-FT'; the software maker's own Mk7 project page reports 'Stage 1+ Gains: + 70hp / 48tq'; and an intake maker's test of a Mk7 GTI already on a Stage 1 tune showed about 260 hp at the wheels on its dyno.
cases.checkNote: Second-reader search did not find the 207 / 282 whp figures or the 43 lb-ft gain on any page, so they rest on the first reader's single summary of a seller's write-up; a similar-sized gain ('+ 70hp / 48tq') on the software maker's own Mk7 project page means the size is not contradicted, but it is not independently verified either.

ruleOfThumb.claim: Boost adds roughly 7% power per psi over naturally aspirated (1 psi is about 1/14.7 = 6.8% of sea-level atmosphere), i.e. hp x (14.7 + boost) / 14.7; an idealised figure that ignores knock, fuel-flow and turbo-efficiency limits.
ruleOfThumb.publisher: Corvette Forum (forum post); same 7%-per-pound figure in eHow 'Horsepower Vs. Boost Pressure'
ruleOfThumb.note: Quoted: '~ 1 psi boost = 6.8% horsepower max (1/14.7 = 6.8%)' and 'a turbo will increase horsepower by about 7 percent per pound of boost over a naturally aspirated configuration'. Check against Civic Si case: 18.87 -> 22.49 psi predicts about +10.8%; measured +7.4% whp, +12.7% torque. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

ruleOfThumb.claim: On a stock-turbo car an off-the-shelf tune raises torque much more than peak power: COBB's Focus ST Stage 1 91-octane map lists +1% HP / +22% TQ at peak and +4% HP / +27% TQ at maximum, with ~21.5 psi peak boost tapering to ~13.5 psi by the 6,800 rpm redline.
ruleOfThumb.publisher: COBB Tuning, Ford Focus ST Map Notes (tuner's own data)
ruleOfThumb.note: Manufacturer claim. Consistent with this page's measured cases (FK8 +7% whp / +17.5% torque; S3 Magazine EcoBoost +4% whp / +15% torque). Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

ruleOfThumb.claim: About 25 psi is the practical limit of the stock EcoBoost Mustang turbo hardware; common pump-gas tunes run around 22 psi.
ruleOfThumb.publisher: AmericanMuscle (retailer); Holley states its tunes raise boost up to 22 psi
ruleOfThumb.note: Retailer guidance, attributed via search summary ('AmericanMuscle cites a rule of thumb that 25 psi is the stock-hardware limit'). Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

ruleOfThumb.claim: There is no universal Stage 1 percentage: the gain depends on the engine and on how conservatively it was calibrated at the factory; turbo engines gain more than naturally aspirated ones because the tune can raise boost as well as timing and fuel.
ruleOfThumb.publisher: HP Academy, 'What Is a Stage 1 Tune?' (attribution from summary)
ruleOfThumb.note: The summary did not tie each phrase to a single URL with certainty; HP Academy was the lead result. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

ruleOfThumb.claim: Compare tune gains only on the same dyno, same fuel and same day: repeat pulls of one car on one dyno vary, stock baselines for one model span 30+ whp across shops (A90 Supra roughly 310-345 whp), and some modern ECUs adapt after a flash so the first post-tune pull can overstate the gain.
ruleOfThumb.publisher: Grassroots Motorsports forum (ECU adaptation comment); BimmerPost forum ('same car on the same dyno 10 times ... 10 different WHP numbers')
ruleOfThumb.note: Forum comments, quoted: 'modern cars will show an initial power gain after being flashed, then they'll start learning around it and the gains go away.' Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
